description: Shared Renovate policy for knorrlabs and etknorr repositories.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Weekly lockfile refresh picks up transitive updates that no manifest names, in the lockfiles Renovate maintains (npm, uv and others; not go.sum). Safe by construction: every resolved version stays inside the ranges the manifests already allow.

packageRules.description: Safe updates automerge once required CI passes: patch, digest and pin changes for everything.
Minor updates automerge only for packages at 1.0 or later. Under 1.0, semver lets a minor break the API, so those stay reviewed.

Container image minors stay reviewed. A base-image or runtime minor (golang 1.26 to 1.27, alpine 3.24 to 3.25, python 3.14 to 3.15 via .python-version) changes the toolchain or OS the build runs on, and no PR CI here builds those images or runs that Python.
Majors are opt-in from the dashboard, never opened unprompted, and never automerged.

First-party GitHub Actions: automerge every update, majors included, after a shortened quarantine. actions/* is published by GitHub itself off a public repo with a narrow maintainer set, and a bad publish there is noticed within hours rather than days, so three days buys most of the protection the default seven does without leaving CI a week behind. An actions/* major is usually a runtime bump that the PR's own CI exercises; one used only in a deploy or release job is not exercised until that job runs. Scoped to the actions/* namespace on purpose: a third-party action is a different trust question, stays on the default quarantine, and its majors still need dashboard approval.

Docs sites are not shipped: every update under docs/**, majors included, opens without dashboard approval and automerges once the docs build passes. A docs major that breaks the build stops on the required check; one that only changes rendering lands, which is the accepted trade-off for not hand-merging docs churn.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes skip the quarantine and are labelled for triage. They follow the same automerge rules as any other update.
